descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-05 Keeping Data Secure / Real-PHI Readiness Gate · S15 Convex plan tier of the production team is the BAA-eligible tier

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U4 The Convex plan tier is the BAA-eligible tier: the actual account plan supports the BAA, not just that a BAA document exists. … (UAT OAT-05; TFA-92568 AC 9; TFA-92568 Product 2; TFA-94703 B1; TFA-94703 AC 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-92568 in progress; TFA-94703 development backlog

Test design technique: Happy path (happy-path) — Walk the normal flow exactly as the UAT / ticket words it; everything it names has to show up.

Given Someone with admin access to the Convex team that owns the production deployment (Venkata Technologies per TFA-94703; Topflight should have admin access)

When Capture the team's billing/plan page, dated, and the Convex BAA. Note which plan the BAA requires and which team signed it.

Then The plan on the team is the tier the Convex BAA names as eligible (TFA-94703 says Pro). The BAA was signed for this same team. Topflight is an admin on it.

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-05 step 4 'not just that a BAA document exists, but that the actual account plan supports it', TFA-92568 AC 9 and TFA-94703 B1. A lower tier, a trial, or a BAA on a different team is a Fail. The dev team is judged per Q12.

Where it ran: dev; test method CONFIG · Config check; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S15 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-05.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: dev — dev deployment, build e02167f (Deploy Convex, 2026-10-12T18:24:27Z); account and address are not written into the report; run folder runs/2026-10-14-dev.

Test method: CONFIG · Config check; secondary: DOC · Document check — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: dev.
